terminology.suggestion: rapid population growth driven by restricted access to healthcare, education, and reproductive rights
terminology.why: This locates the problem in the number of people rather than the systems restricting rights.

terminology.suggestion: voluntary family planning access or reproductive rights
terminology.why: This is the coercive frame PM explicitly rejects, except when describing historical or external language.

terminology.suggestion: the right to decide if and when to have children
terminology.why: This treats reproductive decisions as something to manage rather than a matter of autonomy.

terminology.suggestion: countries where rapid population growth compounds existing pressures
terminology.why: This frames countries and people as the problem.

terminology.suggestion: systems that deny people access to rights, healthcare, and education
sustainable population as a consequence of rights being secured
terminology.why: In public copy this sounds managerial and target-led. It can be acceptable in defined technical internal contexts.

terminology.suggestion: freedom from targets, pressure, or coercion
terminology.why: Targets are incompatible with PM's rights-based position.
This frames fertility as something institutions manage.

terminology.suggestion: sustainable population as a consequence of rights being secured
terminology.why: This implies PM is seeking fewer people rather than secured rights.

terminology.suggestion: her choice or voluntary decisions made with full access to services
terminology.why: Smaller families must not be framed as PM's goal.

terminology.suggestion: Name the coercive history explicitly if referencing it: the discredited population bomb narrative.
terminology.why: Catastrophist people-as-problem framing PM rejects; usable only when named as the framing being refuted.

terminology.suggestion: rapid population growth driven by restricted access to healthcare, education, and reproductive rights
voluntary family planning access and reproductive rights
terminology.why: Frames people as a quantity for institutions to manage.

terminology.suggestion: Name the actual crisis: a rights crisis, a healthcare-funding crisis, an access crisis.
terminology.why: Urgency attached to population itself is the gateway back to coercion logic.

terminology.suggestion: In public copy, frame outcomes through rights and wellbeing, not economic yield from demography.
terminology.why: Legitimate in technical policy contexts when defined; in public copy it values people by economic output.

terminology.suggestion: Permitted only after a rights anchor has been established in the same piece; never as a headline or hook.
terminology.why: Used as a lead, this reproduces population-first framing under a compliant phrase.

patternChecks.suggestion: Frame the issue around reproductive autonomy and access, not demographic targets.
patternChecks.why: This suggests people or countries should change fertility outcomes.

patternChecks.suggestion: Women must be able to make reproductive decisions freely, with access to the services they are owed.
patternChecks.why: PM must never tell anyone to have more or fewer children.

patternChecks.pattern: \b(family planning|contraception|reproductive rights|girls'? education)\b[\s\S]{0,60}\b(climate solution|save the planet|solve climate|reduce emissions|cut emissions)\b
patternChecks.suggestion: State that rights, healthcare, and education are ends in themselves; environmental benefits are consequences, not the justification.
patternChecks.why: This risks treating women and girls as instruments for environmental outcomes.

patternChecks.pattern: \b(poor countries|developing countries|africa|the global south)\b[\s\S]{0,70}\b(too many children|too many people|threat|burden|problem)\b
patternChecks.suggestion: Name the structural barriers: underinvestment in healthcare, education, reproductive rights, and economic security.
patternChecks.why: This can blame countries or communities rather than systems.

patternChecks.pattern: \b(we are committed to|population matters believes|population matters is pleased to|empowering women and girls|sustainable future for all|working in partnership with communities)\b
patternChecks.suggestion: Lead with the person, evidence, claim, or recommendation instead of generic institutional language.
patternChecks.why: This sounds like generic charity copy rather than PM's specific voice.

patternChecks.suggestion: Name the source, date, geography, and what the source actually supports.
patternChecks.why: PM copy needs source fidelity, especially on contested evidence.

patternChecks.pattern: ^(?:(?!reproductive rights|her choice|bodily autonomy|voluntary family planning|access to (?:contraception|healthcare|education)|right to decide)[\s\S]){0,240}\b(?:population (?:growth|pressure|numbers|size)|birth\s*rates?|fertility\s*rates?|demographic (?:change|pressure|trends)|climate (?:change|crisis|breakdown)|emissions)\b
patternChecks.suggestion: Open with the rights anchor - a person, her choice, or the system restricting access - before any population or environmental framing.
patternChecks.why: Rights framing must lead every piece. Population or environmental framing in the first 240 characters without a preceding rights anchor inverts PM's sequence.
patternChecks.note: Suppress if the match is clearly inside quotation marks or within rejection context such as reject, refute, myth, wrong, or narrative.

patternChecks.pattern: \b(climate (?:solution|action|lever|tool|fix)|solution to climate|fight(?:ing)? climate change|reduce (?:carbon |global )?emissions|save the planet|protect biodiversity)\b[\s\S]{0,80}\b(contraception|family planning|reproductive rights|girls'? education|educating (?:girls|women)|empower(?:ing)? women)\b
patternChecks.suggestion: Rights, healthcare, and education are ends in themselves; environmental benefits are consequences, not the justification.
patternChecks.why: Catches reversed instrumentalisation such as the best climate solution is girls' education.

patternChecks.pattern: \bempower(?:ing|ment of)?\s+(?:women|girls|women and girls)\b[\s\S]{0,50}\b(?:to|in order to|so that|as a way to)\b[\s\S]{0,60}\b(?:reduce|lower|cut|curb|slow|stabilise|stabilize|population growth slows?)\b
patternChecks.suggestion: Women's autonomy is not a means to anything. State the right; describe demographic outcomes only as consequences, separately.
patternChecks.why: Empowering women to reduce X makes women instruments of a demographic or environmental goal.

patternChecks.pattern: \b(ticking (?:time ?)?bomb|time bomb|before it'?s too late|running out of time|spiralling out of control|point of no return|crisis point)\b[\s\S]{0,80}\b(population|birth\s*rates?|fertility)\b|\b(population|birth\s*rates?|fertility)\b[\s\S]{0,80}\b(ticking (?:time ?)?bomb|time bomb|before it'?s too late|running out of time|spiralling out of control|point of no return)\b
patternChecks.suggestion: Replace urgency idiom with the specific, evidenced harm of restricted rights - named source, named system.
patternChecks.why: Catastrophist urgency attached to population is the rhetorical engine of coercive policy.

patternChecks.suggestion: Name the system: restricted rights, underfunded healthcare, inequality, policy failure.
Frame the choice, not the number: where women gain genuine choice, they use it on their own terms.
patternChecks.why: Celebrating the demographic outcome itself converts a consequence into a target.

patternChecks.pattern: \b(africa|the global south|developing countries|low-income countries|poorest countries)\b[\s\S]{0,120}\b(emissions|climate change|environmental (?:pressure|breakdown|degradation|damage)|biodiversity loss|deforestation)\b
patternChecks.suggestion: State the consumption asymmetry in the same piece: the heaviest environmental burden comes from the wealthiest people and nations.
patternChecks.why: Linking Global South demography to environmental harm without the asymmetry leaves communities implicitly carrying the blame.
patternChecks.note: Suppress if consumption, wealthiest, or richest appears near the match.

patternChecks.suggestion: Domestic service pressure is a policy and investment story. Never connect it to migration or birth rates.
patternChecks.why: The Anxious Citizens co-option route: scarcity framing drifting into anti-migrant, people-as-pressure territory.
